# Instructions

Implement a RESTful API for tracking IOUs.

Four roommates have a habit of borrowing money from each other frequently, and have trouble remembering who owes whom, and how much.

Your task is to implement a simple [RESTful API][restful-wikipedia] that receives [IOU][iou]s as POST requests, and can deliver specified summary information via GET requests.

## API Specification

### User object

```json
{
  "name": "Adam",
  "owes": {
    "Bob": 12.0,
    "Chuck": 4.0,
    "Dan": 9.5
  },
  "owed_by": {
    "Bob": 6.5,
    "Dan": 2.75
  },
  "balance": "<(total owed by other users) - (total owed to other users)>"
}
```

### Methods

| Description              | HTTP Method | URL    | Payload Format                                                            | Response w/o Payload                   | Response w/ Payload                                                             |
| ------------------------ | ----------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| List of user information | GET         | /users | `{"users":["Adam","Bob"]}`                                                | `{"users":<List of all User objects>}` | `{"users":<List of User objects for <users> (sorted by name)}`                  |
| Create user              | POST        | /add   | `{"user":<name of new user (unique)>}`                                    | N/A                                    | `<User object for new user>`                                                    |
| Create IOU               | POST        | /iou   | `{"lender":<name of lender>,"borrower":<name of borrower>,"amount":5.25}` | N/A                                    | `{"users":<updated User objects for <lender> and <borrower> (sorted by name)>}` |

## Other Resources

- [REST API Tutorial][restfulapi]
- Example RESTful APIs
  - [GitHub][github-rest]
  - [Reddit][reddit-rest]

[restful-wikipedia]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer
[iou]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOU
[github-rest]: https://developer.github.com/v3/
[reddit-rest]: https://web.archive.org/web/20231202231149/https://www.reddit.com/dev/api/
[restfulapi]: https://restfulapi.net/

Use the instructions above to complete `rest_api.py`. Keep the existing function and class names: tests you cannot see import them. Use only the Python standard library.

tool_calls.arguments:
{"summary": "I've written the IOU API in `rest_api.py`, keeping the `RestAPI` class and its `get`/`post` methods. A quick manual run gave the expected results, but the project has no test files, so it hasn't been run against the hidden tests.

- **`GET /users`** returns every user, or only the names listed in the payload, sorted by name.
- **`POST /add`** creates a new user and returns its record. It refuses a name that already exists.
- **`POST /iou`** records a loan and returns the updated lender and borrower, sorted by name. Each pair of users has only one debt between them: a new loan first cancels out any debt running the other way, and if that brings it to exactly zero, the entry is removed from both users.
- **Format:** payloads can be JSON strings or dicts, and responses are JSON strings. `balance` is worked out as (total owed by others) − (total owed to others).
- **Errors:** an unknown URL, an unknown user, or someone lending to themselves raises a `ValueError`.

**How I checked it:** I ran a short script on a two-user database with a series of IOUs. The debt shrank, flipped direction, then grew, and the balances matched each time. Adding a user, getting a filtered list and getting from an empty database all worked too."}
